# Wall St opens higher as chip stocks rebound, Middle East tensions ease

By Thomson Reuters Jun 8, 2026 | 8:35 AM

June 8 (Reuters) – Wall Street’s main indexes opened ​higher on ‌Monday, bouncing back from a sharp selloff in the ‌prior ​session, ⁠aided by ⁠a recovery in chip stocks and signs of easing ​tensions in the Middle ⁠East.

The ⁠Dow Jones Industrial ​Average rose 130.5 ​points, or 0.26%, ‌to 50,997.23. The S&P 500 rose 56.8 ⁠points, or 0.77%, to 7,440.57, while the ⁠Nasdaq ‌Composite rose ⁠355.6 points, ​or ‌1.38%, to 26,065.071 ​at the ⁠opening bell.

(Reporting by Joel Jose in Bengaluru; Editing by Devika ​Syamnath)--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# How major US stock indexes fared Friday, 2/28/2025

The Associated Press

February 28, 2025 1 min read

Wall Street closed its dreary February on a brighter note, as U.S. stock indexes rallied.

The S&P 500 jumped 1.6% Friday to trim its loss for the month, enough to make it the worst since only December instead of since April. The Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 1.4%, and the Nasdaq composite added 1.6%.

Nvidia jumped to recover a chunk of its steep loss from Thursday, which helped lift the market. Treasury yields sank after a report said that inflation decelerated a bit last month but also that U.S. consumers also cut back on their spending. Asian stock indexes tumbled amid worries about tariffs.

On Friday:

The S&P 500 rose 92.93 points, or 1.6%, to 5,954.50.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 601.41 points, or 1.4%, to 43,840.91.

The Nasdaq composite rose 302.86 points, or 1.6%, to 18,847.28.

The Russell 2000 index of smaller companies rose 23.41 points, or 1.1%, to 2,163.07.

For the week:

The S&P 500 is down 58.63 points, or 1%.

The Dow is up 412.89 points, or 1%.

The Nasdaq is down 676.73 points, or 3.5%.

The Russell 2000 is down 32.28 points, or 1.5%.

For the year:

The S&P 500 is up 72.87 points, or 1.2%.

The Dow is up 1,296.69 points, or 3%.

The Nasdaq is down 463.51 points, or 2.4%.

The Russell 2000 is down 67.09 points, or 3%.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

AI stocks halt their brutal, worldwide sell-off as Wall Street trims its loss for the week
Date: Fri Nov  6 00:43:24 2026 UTC
Location: New York, New York, United States

NEW YORK (AP) - AI stocks bounced back Friday and recovered some of their sell-off from the last two days. The rest of the U.S. stock market was mixed, though, following a whirlwind few days of Wall Street trying to sort out what this week's sweeping victories by Democrats in the U.S. midterm elections will mean for the economy.
The S&P 500 rose 0.3% and trimmed its loss for the week to 2.7%, which was its worst since President Donald Trump shook markets in April 2025 with his "Liberation Day" tariffs. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 237 points, or 0.5%, and the Nasdaq composite climbed 1.1%. 
The relative steadiness for Wall Street halted what had been a worldwide tumble for stocks. Indexes dropped 6% in Tokyo and in Seoul following the U.S. market's plunge on Thursday. European indexes have fewer stocks tied to the artificial-intelligence industry, but Germany's DAX nevertheless lost 1.9%.
In the meantime, companies in the industry still see strong growth. 
IREN, a company that delivers data centers, compute and software for AI training, reported stronger results for the latest quarter than analysts expected. Its stock jumped 20%, and it also announced two new contracts signed since the end of the quarter.
Lam Research, a company whose equipment and services help make semiconductors, climbed 8.2% after announcing a program to send up to $25 billion to its investors by buying back shares of its own stock.
That helped other stocks that have benefited from the build-out of AI data centers recover some of their own sharp losses. CoreWeave, which rents out access to AI chips to customers over the cloud, rose 6.3%. Micron Technology, which sells memory for computers, climbed 5.1%.
Outside of AI, the U.S. stock market was mixed, and more stocks fell within the S&P 500 than rose.
Axon Enterprise tumbled 18.2% after the seller of Tasers reported weaker results for the latest quarter than analysts expected. It also announced a $1.2 billion investment in Skydio, a drone technology company. 
Charter Communications sank 6.2% after the internet and video provider reported a loss for the latest quarter, when analysts were expecting a profit. 
All told, the S&P 500 rose 23.13 points to 7,376.86. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dipped 237.33 to 51,285.73, and the Nasdaq composite climbed 264.43 to 24,579.42.
Despite all its vicious swings this week, the S&P 500 remains only 5.7% below its all-time high, which was set last month.
In the bond market, Treasury yields held firmer following sharp drops earlier in the week triggered by tumbling stock prices and hopes that split control of Washington could limit how much more the U.S. government adds to its debt. 
The yield on the 10-year Treasury rose to 4.86% from 4.84% late Thursday. It had topped 5.30% last month when worries about inflation, higher interest rates and rising government debt were spiking.
Helping to support yields was a report released Friday morning showing U.S. employers hired many more workers last month than economists expected. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
